messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: production kv-prefix cache size spike in prod-us-east-1. total_kv_bytes went from ~43GB -> ~472GB in 3m, continuous-batcher queue length growing, p99 gen latency up 10x. auto-escalation to ops-pager (INC-2026-0421).

emma_ops: ack, I'm in. paging runtime and tokenizer leads. grabbing traces.

sanjay_oncall: joining. quick triage: saw a template rollout ~12m ago that changed prompt templates -> likely more unique prefixes. also rolling batch config push 10m ago (batching.max_prompts 64 -> 256). suspect combined effect = cache amplification.

dina_sre: +1. prefix cache key is "prefix_hash = hash(prefix_template || prompt_hash)" — if tokenizer changed tokenization boundaries, prompt_hash diverges and we might not hit prefix dedupe. also larger batch sizes multiply prefix writes because continuous batching flushes more unique keys per commit.

support_lead: customer impact: three large customers (cust-fin, cust-search, cust-chat) reporting elevated tail latency and some 5xx traces in our proxy. CS ticket count rising. marking "incident - customer-impact" flag.

emma_ops: mitigation plan: 1) quick reduce batching to reduce write amplification 2) disable prefix cache writes for canary models to stop growth 3) patch template rollout to use stable tokenization boundaries or revert to previous tokenizer version. executing 1 now.

emma_ops: running: `redwoodctl config set --scope prod --route continuous-batcher.max_prompts 64`

deploybot: rolling config change started: continuous-batcher pool -> 5 nodes rolling. canary on 2 nodes first.

deploybot: canary result: node-1 OK, node-2 OK, config apply 2/2. rolling to remaining 3 nodes.

emma_ops: changed `max_prompts` back to 64 across prod. monitoring kv growth.

sanjay_oncall: seeing immediate drop in new prefix insert rate from ~120k/s -> ~18k/s. KV size delta still high but trending down. p99 latency from 1200ms -> 380ms. partial win.

dina_sre: we should stop writes from malformed tokenizer variants. adding short-term gate: env REDWOOD_PREFIX_CACHE_WRITE=false for model group "canary-*". command: `redwoodctl env set prod canary-templates REDWOOD_PREFIX_CACHE_WRITE false`

emma_ops: applied gate to canary group. also temporarily increased kv-ttl evict sweep frequency to 30s to reclaim space: `redwoodctl maintenance set --kv-ttl-sweep 30s`

support_lead: notifying top customers: sent outbound note to cust-fin (they acknowledged), putting status page update.

ben_product: flagged this as high priority for postmortem. note that the template changes were shipped to address a customer request; need to sync.

emma_ops: next step: roll back template change or rehash keys using tokenizer version in key derivation. prefer rehash to preserve cache semantics. quick patch: add tokenizer_version to prefix hash input. will try small patch on canary.

emma_ops: patch snippet:
```
// quick hotfix: include tokenizer version in prefix hash
string prefix_key = H(prefix_template + "|" + tokenizer_version + "|" + template_revision);
KV.put(prefix_key, cached_prefix);
```
Applying to canary runtime.

deploybot: hotfix deploy to canary started -> 1/1 success. smoke tests: ok.

sanjay_oncall: canary metrics: prefix write rate stable, insert collisions down. rolling to remainder.

deploybot: rolling to remaining nodes started. 3/3 success.

emma_ops: monitoring: total_kv_bytes plateaued at ~480GB and now decaying. p99 latency back to ~150ms. no new customer 5xx reports last 10m.

dina_sre: root cause summary (prelim): 1) template rollout introduced more unique prefixes per request 2) tokenizer boundary differences increased effective key cardinality 3) aggressive batch config increased per-commit writes (amplification) -> cache blowup.

support_lead: update: cust-fin reported degraded UX for 22m, they saw sporadic timeouts but no data loss. opened follow-up with cust success.

emma_ops: current status: mitigations applied (batching reduced, writes gated for canaries, tokenizer-aware hash in place, kv-ttl sweep increased). metrics look healthy. incident status -> "mitigated". continuing monitoring for 60m.

sanjay_oncall: handing off to emma_ops for the rest of the watch. I'm available if it re-escalates.

emma_ops: taking handoff. logging owners: emma_ops, dina_sre. will file postmortem and timeline, and coordinate follow-up fixes: - stronger pre-rollout check for prefix cardinality - automatic batch config safety limits - snapshot/restore for affected kv shards.

ben_product: adding product note: we need guardrails in template UI to warn about tokenization explosion.

incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-0421 marked MITIGATED by emma_ops at 2026-03-15T13:47:05Z. Postmortem owners assigned.

emma_ops: thanks all :thumbsup: — closing channel when watch window ends.
